name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 29

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Roamer we can perhaps take to be one who wants to get on

definitions.text: one who wants to get on

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters given are only one possible arrangement, so the solver may reorder them

explanation.surface: A wanderer is taken to be an ambitious go-getter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we can' does double duty in the surface but all eleven letters of 'Roamer we can' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman pursuing a professional path is ambitious, keen to rise and advance at work.

clue.text: Marks oddball as first one to join the Civil Service

blocks.note: an oddball is a real character, an eccentric
first is written 1st, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An eccentric is marked out as the first to join the Civil Service.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARACTER + IST + I + CS spells CHARACTERISTICS; 'as' and 'to join the' only glue the pieces together.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguishing features or traits of a person or thing are its marks, the qualities that identify it.

clue.text: Think to rise in debt having started again

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned backwards
'in' places one piece inside the other one named after it

blocks.note: being in the red means being in debt

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they will climb into debt now that spending has begun again.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'in the red' is being in debt, the convention behind the outer piece; the reversed word for think sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resumed is the past participle for picking something up again after a pause, so it means having started again.

clue.text: Somebody senior providing the translations

blocks.note: German for 'the', a second translation of the same word

explanation.surface: An older colleague supplies the translations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the translations' asks for 'the' in two foreign languages: Spanish EL and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a person older or higher in standing than others, especially in a church or community.

clue.text: Government offices providing one way to Parliament

blocks.note: first meaning: the British civil service and its ministries, named after the street they line
second meaning: the London street that runs down to the Houses of Parliament

explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is a London street lined with government departments, leading from Trafalgar Square to Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the street stands by metonymy for the ministries housed along it, and the street literally leads to Westminster.

clue.text: Good books on human error in police operation

indicators.note: an error puts letters in the wrong order, so the word before it is rearranged
in an across-style reading 'on' means placed after, so the books come second

blocks.note: the New Testament, books of the Good Book

explanation.surface: Bible study is blamed for a human slip during a police operation.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament, is a standard crossword abbreviation; here it goes after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised search by police for a wanted person is a manhunt, a typical kind of operation.

clue.text: Firm operated by one who shall be nameless need not concern us

definitions.note: a clause; the answer fits as 'it's ___'

blocks.note: belonging to no one, a person who goes unnamed

explanation.surface: A company run by an anonymous owner is none of our affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The firm is owned by nobody, making it the nobody's firm; the phrase is the idiom 'it's nobody's business'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is nobody's business means it is private, not anyone else's affair to worry about.

clue.text: Crime kept quiet by a church person

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: A clergyman hushes up a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The quiet letter is placed by the crime, at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: A parson is a parish priest or clergyman, someone employed by the church.

clue.text: Almost starting now before time

indicators.note: 'starting' points to only the opening letter of the word after it

blocks.note: early means ahead of the appointed time

explanation.surface: Someone is nearly beginning now, ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are synonyms, both meaning not quite or very close to.

clue.text: Piled up in the same sad tangle

indicators.note: in a tangle things are twisted and mixed, so these letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Things heaped up in a sorry, familiar mess.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a large quantity, so something amassed has been heaped together.

clue.text: Mean one to belong in a different state

indicators.note: a word put into another state or form has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A miserly person wants to live in another American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a place to belong, but the phrase signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the sense of base or dishonourable matches ignoble, lacking nobility of character.

clue.text: Creature in a chieftain’s power

indicators.note: 'in' says the creature sits inside the following word's letters

blocks.note: letters three to five of the word

explanation.surface: An animal held under a tribal leader's control.
explanation.walkthrough: An eft is a newt, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a small amphibian, a young newt, so it is a living creature.

clue.text: Keep starting to speak

blocks.note: surface reading: repeatedly beginning to say something, as in a meeting
setter's reading: getting stuck on the first sounds of words over and over

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone trying to get a word in; really it describes a speech impediment.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker with this impediment repeats initial sounds involuntarily, so they keep beginning words without finishing them.

clue.text: Old French money causing agitation when war ends in South America

definitions.note: the clue names where the country is, not the country itself

indicators.note: 'ends' points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the écu was an old French coin

explanation.surface: Old French currency stirs up trouble when a war is over in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a country on the Pacific coast of the continent, straddling the equator, which gives it its name.

clue.text: One that's likely to be cracked

definitions.text: One that's likely to be cracked

blocks.clueFragment: One that's likely to be cracked
blocks.note: surface reading: a person likely to go mad, to crack up
setter's reading: a hard-shelled seed that is broken open to eat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' also means crazy, and the answer is slang for a crazy person too.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-shelled kernels such as walnuts are opened by cracking, and the word is also slang for a madman.

clue.text: It's believed to follow the old lady

blocks.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: Supposedly the right thing is to go after one's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lady' is slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of principles held as true by a church or group, something accepted on faith.

clue.text: Go-ahead given with warning for inexperienced youth

blocks.note: a green light gives permission to proceed
a car horn sounds a warning

explanation.surface: Permission comes with a caution for a young novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenhorn is a raw novice, someone new and naive to a job or place.

clue.text: Bad-tempered enough to try you at first

indicators.note: 'at first' keeps only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone is cranky enough to try your patience from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy describes someone easily irritated and short-tempered, cross in manner.

clue.text: Give up in favour of a shot

blocks.note: a go is an attempt or shot

explanation.surface: Abandon something in preference for having a try.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to do without or renounce something, which is to give it up.

clue.text: Spies don’t quite fall about for beauty treatment

indicators.note: not quite finishing a word means its last letter is dropped
'about' means going around, so one piece wraps the other

explanation.surface: Secret agents nearly tumble over for a spa session.
explanation.walkthrough: The CIA is the American Central Intelligence Agency, a crossword staple for spies.
explanation.definitionFit: A facial is a cosmetic treatment for the face, cleansing and massaging the skin.

clue.text: Manner of one with nothing to hide outside

blocks.note: someone with nothing to hide is open
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: The bearing of an honest person, out in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outdoors, not under cover, so it means outside.

clue.text: Ruffled lace giving final moment of striking effect

indicators.note: ruffled means disturbed and disarranged, so the word after it is jumbled
'final' keeps only the closing letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A frilled lace trim gives a dress its dazzling finishing touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliance or conspicuous success, a showy effect that impresses.

clue.text: Wrest it out of one that isn’t honest

indicators.note: 'out' here means wrong or awry, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Force a confession out of a dishonest person.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a cheat or swindler, someone who twists the truth or a deal.

clue.text: Don't start to heat a vessel

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter of the word is left off

blocks.note: to burn is to heat strongly

explanation.surface: Instruction not to begin warming a kettle.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a large metal container for heating tea water, or a vase, both kinds of vessel.

clue.text: Close the way up during dark periods

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means reading from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Shutting a road during the hours of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a verb about the road but is the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: Nights are the hours between dusk and dawn, the dark part of each day.

clue.text: Where water may be held back behind the Channel Islands

indicators.note: 'behind' puts the piece it follows at the rear, after the islands

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Water is kept back off the Channel Islands, like a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reads as one phrase, but 'held' ends the definition and 'back' is the wordplay. The Channel Islands are British islands off Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, such as the one above a toilet or in a loft.

clue.text: South African one needing fish leaving port

blocks.note: the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A South African needs a fish before the boat goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing is a scheduled departure of a ship, its setting out from harbour.

clue.text: Minister with imperfections shown up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A government minister has his flaws exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was a British Labour cabinet minister, Home Secretary and Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Jack Straw held several senior ministerial posts in the UK.

clue.text: This way you can leave the woman to be a success

indicators.note: leaving something behind means those letters are taken away from the word

blocks.note: a woman referred to as her

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to walk out on a woman and still come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: HITHER loses HER from its end to leave HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a popular success, such as a song or show that sells well.

clue.text: Wild music — you might have a go at it

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled and disordered, so the letters later in the clue are jumbled

explanation.surface: Frenzied music that anyone might attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: Agitato is an Italian marking for an agitated, restless passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is a musical direction meaning played in a restless, excited way, and names such a passage.

clue.text: Somewhere to hide in connection with pleasure

explanation.surface: A hideaway linked with enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet, secluded refuge where one can withdraw from others.

clue.text: They're said to be used with powerful effect

definitions.text: They're said to be used with powerful effect

explanation.surface: Some remarks are reputed to have a forceful impact.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and within it the things said and the word for powerful build the phrase, powerful placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful or angry language, such as harsh rebukes, is spoken to make a powerful impact.
